extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for language modeling consisting of text extracted from Wikipedia articles that fit the Good or Featured article criteria.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Articles fitting the Good or Featured criteria were selected and their text was extracted using the Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Words outside of the constructed vocabulary (words with a count below 3) were mapped to the <unk> token.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Specific sections featuring lists and minor HTML bugs were removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Normalization and tokenization using the Moses tokenizer, augmented to split numbers. Words with a count below 3 were discarded and mapped to an <unk> token.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Penn Treebank dataset has limitations as its tokens are all lower case, stripped of any punctuation, and limited to a vocabulary of only 10k words, making it unrealistic for real language use. For the WikiText dataset, extracting raw text is nontrivial due to macros, and specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Language modeling benchmark with Training, Validation, and Testing splits.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We selected articles only fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: Once extracted, specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default. Other minor bugs, such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from the HTML, were also removed. Mathematical formulae and L ATEX code, were replaced with <formula> tokens.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007), slightly augmented to further split numbers... a vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3. Words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the <unk> token
